# Foreman

> Foreman runs each copy of a repo as its own devcontainer environment on boxes you own: a control plane (Phoenix) sends commands to an agent on each box, which clones the repo and brings up its compose-based devcontainer, unprivileged, with Tailscale, secrets, git identity and GitHub credentials layered on.

If you're getting a repo ready to run on Foreman, read "Making a repo work with Foreman" first, especially "What trips a port up": the remote user doesn't run as the uid the image sets, HOME volumes keep stale state, committed lockfiles pin features, and only the devcontainer service is on the tailnet.

## Getting a repo ready

- [Making a repo work with Foreman](docs/setup/repos.md): what Foreman adds, what a box refuses, what to remove, what trips a port up, secrets, coming from Codespaces
